topic: Geiss triplanar world-space cliff projection vs top-down planar UV cliff stretching rig
topic_zh: Geiss 三平面正交世界投影（Triplanar Mapping）对比朴素顶视平面 UV 悬崖绝壁纵向拉丝
scope: Deterministic Ryan Geiss (NVIDIA GPU Gems 3, 2007) conformal triplanar world-space projection (D_tri = D_0 * (N_x^2 + N_y^2 + N_z^2)) versus naive top-down planar XZ projection (D_planar = D_0 * cos(theta)) and 64-step 3D cliff arc-length parametric quadrature across 17 cliff slope angle stations (theta in [5 deg, 85 deg]). No neural texture inpainting execution.

protocol.function: D_tri(θ) = D₀ · (N_y·cos θ + N_x·sin θ) = D₀ · (N_y² + N_x²) ≡ 1.0000 → 0.0000 Cliff Stretch Across 5°..85°

robustness.name: Sampled 17 cliff slope stations preserve unit texel density without vertical UV streak stretching

good_fit: Open-world terrain cliffs, Marching Cubes voxel caves, procedural SDF rock formations, and architectural ruins without manual UV unwrapping
Eliminating 5.76× (80°) to 11.47× (85°) vertical texture streak stretching on steep heightfield slopes
Blending orthogonal YZ, XZ, and XY world-plane projections directly from world normal N without inverse trigonometry
Pairing with Reoriented Normal Mapping / Whiteout blending (Round 65) for tangent-free normal maps
not_for: Skinned deforming characters where world-space coordinates swim across moving limbs (use rest-pose object space or UV unwrapping)
Single flat horizontal floors where 1-tap XZ planar projection is already exact
Neural texture synthesis or diffusion inpainting
Unique non-tiling hero decals requiring custom 2D UV parameterization
